case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1987] 1 Sri L.R. 293

clause.text: Punishment can only be imposed by a competent court and detention before trial is not punishment.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner’s detention pending investigation constituted unlawful punishment in violation of Article 13(4).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner argued that his continued detention was illegal and amounted to punishment without trial.
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents stated the detention was authorized for further investigation under Emergency Regulations.
key_facts: Petitioner detained from 22 May 1985 to at least 11 June 1985 pending investigation.
No affidavits from respondents explicitly stated detention was for further investigation.
Magistrate was informed on 25 June 1985 that investigation was ongoing and extracts were submitted to Attorney-General.
Court relied on previous case Yasapalitha Nanayakkara v. Henry Perera regarding lawful detention for investigation.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(4) prohibits detention as punishment before trial; detention pending investigation is not punishment if lawful and for investigation purposes.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found the detention was for further investigation as authorized by the Inspector-General of Police under Emergency Regulations, thus not unlawful punishment.
principles_established: Detention pending investigation is lawful and not punishment if authorized and for investigation.
Detention without a specified purpose or unknown purpose is unlawful and violates Article 13(4).
precedents_cited: Yasapalitha Nanayakkara v. Henry Perera and Others

outcome.holding: The petitioner’s detention was lawful pending investigation and did not violate Article 13(4).

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: The court addressed whether detention pending investigation constituted unlawful punishment, concluding it did not under Article 13(4) when properly authorized.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Inspector-General of Police authorized detention for offences under Regulation 26, and the Magistrate was informed that investigation was ongoing with extracts submitted to the Attorney-General.
